reference_caption: The Saigon Opera House, an impressive structure built during the French colonial era, stands as a testament to neoclassical architecture. Its ornate facade and prominent arched entrance catch the eye amidst the bustling cityscape, now flanked by modern high-rises. The building's raised floor, positioned above street level, houses both a concert hall and additional furnishings. Originally constructed under the direction of Paul Bourret for the French colonial administration, it has since been renamed the Salle de Concert. Today, the opera house continues to serve its cultural purpose while also incorporating elements of a shop within its interior.
